children: COPENHAGEN, Denmark, October 27, 2026
– Bavarian Nordic A/S
OMX:BAVA

today announced that it will strengthen global preparedness for mpox through a donation of 75,000 doses of its MVA-BN® vaccine to the newly established global mpox vaccine emergency stockpile, helping ensure that protection is available when and where it is needed. The creation of a new stockpile marks an important milestone in global mpox preparedness, helping to ensure timely and equitable access to vaccines and enabling effective outbreak response for communities around the world.

It is managed by the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, a mechanism hosted by WHO that coordinates the allocation and deployment of emergency vaccine supplies to countries responding to outbreaks. Initial funding for the stockpile has been provided by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance.

The donation complements a newly awarded contract to supply 150,000 doses to the stockpile. Bavarian Nordic’s contribution through both vaccine supply and donation reflects its longstanding commitment to global health security and its mission to protect people and communities, and save lives, through vaccines.
Hitesh Sahni, Senior Vice President, Public Preparedness at Bavarian Nordic

, said: “Infectious diseases do not stop at borders, and communities need timely access to protection when outbreaks occur. The establishment of a global mpox vaccine emergency stockpile is an important milestone in strengthening preparedness for future outbreaks. Ensuring timely and equitable access to vaccines is critical to protecting populations and enabling an effective public health response. We are proud to embark on a new collaboration with ICG partners to build a more coordinated and resilient response to the recurring threat of mpox.”
About the smallpox/mpox vaccine

MVA-BN, or Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic, is the only non-replicating mpox vaccine approved in the U.S., Switzerland, Singapore and Mexico (marketed as JYNNEOS®), Canada (marketed as IMVAMUNE®), and the EU/EAA and United Kingdom (marketed as IMVANEX®). It was originally developed as a smallpox vaccine in collaboration with the U.S. government to ensure the supply of a smallpox vaccine for the US population, including immunocompromised individuals who are not recommended vaccination with replicating smallpox vaccines. MVA-BN is now indicated for use for individuals considered at risk for smallpox or mpox infection.

Bavarian Nordic has been a long-term supplier of the vaccine to national stockpiles. During the 2022-2024 mpox outbreaks, the Company supported governments and international organizations by expanding access to the vaccine to more than 70 countries worldwide.

In 2024, MVA-BN received WHO prequalification for the use of the vaccine by individuals aged 12 years and older, enabling procurement through the UN agency focusing on children’s health. More recently, the European Commission approved an extension of the vaccine's marketing authorization in the EU/EEA to include children aged 2 to under 12 years. This expanded indication further helps to address the unmet need for mpox vaccines among younger populations at increased risk of infection.

Bavarian Nordic is working with global partners on additional clinical studies to further expand the availability of MVA-BN for other vulnerable populations. In parallel, the Company is developing new manufacturing processes to allow for scaling of capacity to meet increased demand in the future.
